title: Sensitivity and Specificity of Cytokines in the Diagnosis of Lymphoma-associated HLH
off: The Role of Cytokines in Early Diagnosis, Assessment of Response and Prognosis of Patients With Lymphoma-associated Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis
summary: Lymphoma-associated hemophagocytic lympohistiocytosis is a refractory immune disorder with high mortality. Early identification and diagnosis of lymphoma-associated HLH has become the key to improve the prognosis of lymphoma-associated HLH. Therefore, we conduct a multicenter, prospective, observational clinical study to explore the sensitivity and specificity of cytokines for the early diagnosis of lymphoma-associated HLH.
desc: Lymphoma-associated hemophagocytic lympohistiocytosis is a refractory immune disorder with high mortality. Without early intervention, the median survival time is less than 2 months. Early identification and diagnosis of lymphoma-associated HLH has become the key to improve the prognosis of lymphoma-associated HLH. Therefore, it is urgent to find a method for the early diagnosis of lymphoma-associated HLH. We conduct a multicenter, prospective, observational clinical study to explore the sensitivity and specificity of cytokines for the early diagnosis of lymphoma-associated HLH, and its correlation with disease severity, treatment response, and prognosis.

Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult, gender is not limited.
* Patients with histopathologically confirmed lymphoma who meet HLH-04 diagnostic criteria, and did not receive systemic chemotherapy before enrollment.
* Patients with histopathologically confirmed lymphoma who did not receive systemic chemotherapy before enrollment.
* Informed consent obtained.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients with severe active infections (viral, bacterial, fungal, or parasitic).
* Patients with active autoimmune disease or a history of organ transplantation who are receiving immunosuppressive therapy.
* Patients with other type of malignant tumors within 5 years, except for cured solid tumors.
* Patients planned to receive immunotherapy.
* Pregnant and breastfeeding females.
* History of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection.
* Acute or chronic active hepatitis B or hepatitis C.
* Patients assessed as ineligible for the study by the investigator.

x.titre: Dosage des cytokines pour le diagnostic précoce du lymphome avec HLH
x.question: Le dosage des cytokines permet-il de diagnostiquer précocement un syndrome d'activation macrophagique associé à un lymphome ?
x.contexte:
Le syndrome hémophagocytaire (HLH) est un syndrome d'hyperinflammation grave, souvent déclenché par un lymphome chez l'adulte. Sans prise en charge rapide, la survie médiane est inférieure à 2 mois selon le registre.

Le diagnostic repose sur les critères HLH-04 (fièvre, cytopénies, hyperferritinémie, hypertriglycéridémie, splénomégalie, hémophagocytose, etc.), souvent tardifs ou difficiles à réunir chez un patient atteint de lymphome. Le profil des cytokines (interféron gamma, IL-10, IL-6…) est un marqueur d'activation immunitaire plausible mais mal validé. Cette étude observationnelle prospective chinoise compare des patients atteints de lymphome avec et sans HLH, avant toute chimiothérapie, pour évaluer la sensibilité et la spécificité de ces dosages. Elle explore aussi leur lien avec la gravité, la réponse au traitement et le pronostic. Le promoteur est l'hôpital Beijing Friendship.
x.interet: Un test sanguin simple pourrait faire gagner du temps pour reconnaître un HLH au cours d'un lymphome. Il faciliterait une décision thérapeutique précoce dans une situation à forte mortalité.
x.profil: Des adultes atteints d'un lymphome confirmé, avec ou sans HLH, n'ayant pas reçu de chimiothérapie.
